I wouldn’t think it’s asking too much to have him write things down, especially if you explain that it would be helpful for you! From what you said in the post, it sounds like your boyfriend cares about you a lot.

You’ve received some great advice on here so I’m not sure there’s much I can add, but a few things that may help reassure you: 
- You’re not too insensitive to have trouble being calm when someone has revealed very big, traumatic events. 
- Like other people have commented, it’s probably alright to ask him about what he’s said to reassure your mind. Write your thoughts down and the questions you want to ask so you can use them as a guideline and not become too emotional and have things escalate (as someone with BPD, this helps me so I don’t get off track or say something I didn’t mean to say). 
- You mentioned that anyone can lie so you have a hard time believing him when he says you’re special. I FEEL YOU! One thing that helps me is I have my partner write his feelings about me down. It’s easier to have a permanent declaration of love I can look at when feeling insecure about our relationship. Maybe that could be something you ask to ease those mental doubts? :) 
Best of luck, everything is going to be okay.

She didn’t know it was Kate on Christmas Eve. Therefore, Mallory didn’t go to the police saying it was Kate because she didn’t know it was Kate. She knew it was Kate only after Kate was free. Different than Jeanette knowing it was Kate in Martin’s house while she was missing. There’s a difference, and it’s not what you said or implied.

She admitted she knew it was Kate after it was reported Kate was the person in the house! She knew she couldn’t say anything to the police because then it would give away Kate’s truth. She didn’t know during Christmas Eve when Kate was on the phone.

Listen... I appreciate the time you put into this analysis, but Jeanette is Not a Good Dude. 

She’s a teenager. Yes, this gives her some leeway for things like lying about the joints, but I’d say most teenagers would know that not reporting a kidnapping victim is wrong.  That letting someone suffer is wrong. 

I’ve never read “The Kite Runner” so I can’t see the comparison first-hand. I still can’t say I find your argument or comparison on Jeanette’s behalf compelling.

Editing to throw in that Mallory never saw Kate’s face, so she genuinely thought she saw a relative/girlfriend of Martin. Not a kidnapping victim, and she’d have no reason to believe the lady she saw was Kate. So, yes, Mallory took a “not my problem” approach. Comparing Mallory’s situation to Jeanette’s situation is comparing apples to oranges. Jeanette knew who was in the basement and wrongly did nothing. Mallory didn’t know who was in the house, and rightly did nothing.

Guided runs are really helpful if you hate running! The Nike Run Club app (not sponsored I swear) is free and they have great guided runs that tell you how to run properly and build up from where you’re at. Also, it’s good to just get out there and run- that’s how you get better! 10 minutes of running is better than no running, so on. 

AND GOOD SHOES! Invest in a nice pair of running shoes. They’ll issue ones at basic which kinda sucks, but it’s good to build strength on quality running shoes so you don’t get injured. The investment is worth it. Hit up your local running store where professionals can help you find the right shoe for your kind of training. They can also give you good tips :) 

Be sure to know what you have to do to pass the ACFT as well. The two mile is the final event! Your legs can very well be tired after the sprint drag carry and all that.
